overall: The AG found the Wayland Finance Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating over email on warrant articles and by failing to respond to the complaint, but not for distributing draft minutes by email.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a quorum of members exchanged emails expressing opinions on public business within the Committee's jurisdiction.
allegations.key_passage: The September 9, 2012 and September 10, 2012 emails conveying members' opinions on proposed warrant articles were deliberation, however, and violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Members' emails circulating draft open and executive session minutes before approval were challenged as deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The September 4, 2012 and September 9, 2012 emails sent by Ms. Karlson to the Committee members attaching draft minutes were not deliberation.

allegations.summary: The Committee did not respond to the filed Open Meeting Law complaint within the required time, even after an extension was granted.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Committee never filed a response.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
Publicly release the emails sent in violation of the Open Meeting Law, if not already done, at the Committee's next regular meeting.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution the Committee that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the law. The Committee must also publicly release the emails sent in violation of the Open Meeting Law, if it has not done so already, at its next regular meeting.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
